Metricool: scheduled Mon 2026-10-26 13:00 IG + TikTok
Myth: "AI is smart enough to handle the risk for you."
One thing: the risk is on you, so set guardrails first.
Drive: G:/My Drive/06 Content Creation/ManrajTalks/Carousels/1409-ai-risk-guardrails/
guide: Put limits around an AI tool before it acts, so a mistake costs you little. You need an AI assistant (ChatGPT, Codex or Claude Code) and a clear idea of what the AI is and is not allowed to touch.
1. Write down what the AI is for, and list the actions it must never take on its own, such as sending emails, deleting files, spending money or publishing.
1. Give the AI the least access it needs: a single Google Drive folder or one Notion page, not your whole account.
1. Use a test copy or a draft area first, so early mistakes land somewhere harmless.
1. Add an approval step before anything outward-facing, for example the AI posts its proposed action to Telegram and waits for you to reply yes.
1. Set hard limits where the tool allows them, such as a spending cap, a daily run limit or read-only permissions.
1. Keep a simple log of what the AI did and when, so you can check it and undo it.
1. Review the log after the first few runs, then loosen the limits only where it has behaved well.
Watch out: the AI will not judge risk for you, because the risk stays with you, so set the guardrails before you run it, not after something goes wrong.

```
You are helping me set up guardrails for an AI workflow before I run it. The task I want the AI to do is <describe the task>. The tools I use are <for example ChatGPT, Claude Code, Google Drive, Notion, Telegram>.
Please produce:
1. A list of actions the AI may do on its own, actions that need my approval, and actions it must never do, based on <what could go wrong, for example sending messages, deleting files, spending money>.
2. The minimum permissions and access it needs in each tool, and how to set them up with the tools I named.
3. An approval step for anything outward-facing, using <my approval channel, for example Telegram or email>, where the AI waits for my yes before acting.
4. Hard limits I can set, such as <spending cap, daily run limit, read-only access>.
5. A simple log format recording what the AI did, when, and how to undo it.
Keep it in plain English and use only tools I already have. Start with a short checklist I can follow today, then give any setup steps or code I need. Do not assume the AI will manage risk for me.
```
